name: user-menu
summary: The interactive header ACCOUNT menu — an avatar/initials trigger that opens a dropdown with a user header, account links, an optional theme toggle, and a danger Logout. Self-contained (renders its own trigger + top-layer popover) so it drops into obs-app-header's `user` slot, or stands alone. The turnkey form of the `user-menu` recipe.
selectHint: The header avatar + account dropdown (My Profile / Setup / Docs / theme / Logout)? -> obs-user-menu in the app-header `user` slot. For a generic action menu use obs-menu; for nav use obs-sidebar/obs-side-menu.
whenToUse: The top-right account control of the app shell — the avatar that opens the user's profile links, theme toggle, and Logout. One per app chrome.
insteadOf: obs-menu configured from scratch each time (obs-user-menu is the turnkey version)
putting account links in the sidebar

variants.name: default
variants.what: Avatar (initials) trigger -> header (name + subtitle) + account links + theme toggle + danger Logout.

variants.name: avatar-image
variants.what: An image avatar (the `avatar` src prop) instead of initials.

variants.name: minimal
variants.what: theme-toggle="false" logout="false" -> just the account links.

variants.name: theme-switcher
variants.what: the Dark / Light / Auto SEGMENTED switcher (reuses obs-radio as-button, moon/sun/theme-auto icons); `theme` sets the active segment, a change emits `theme` {value}.
variants.usage: the product default — per-user theme control lives in the account menu

variants.name: placement-start
variants.what: placement="bottom-start" aligns the dropdown to the LEFT of the avatar (default is bottom-end / right).
variants.usage: when the avatar sits away from the right edge

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: matches the app-header avatar; the dropdown is a 240px min-width panel.

states.name: open
states.what: the top-layer dropdown is shown (avatar gets a focus ring); click-outside / Esc closes it.

states.name: hover
states.what: rows highlight on hover; the danger Logout row is red.

name.note: display name shown in the dropdown header.

avatar.note: avatar image src; if empty, initials are shown.

items.note: account links: [{key,label,icon?,href?,danger?,divider?}]. An href renders an <a>; otherwise a button that emits `select`.

theme-toggle.note: show the Dark/Light/Auto theme switcher (a segmented control; the active segment is a --primary pill).

placement.note: align the dropdown to the right (default) or left of the avatar.

theme.note: the current theme selection shown in the Dark/Light/Auto segmented switcher.

manage-theme.note: Built-in theme control. When true (default) picking Dark/Light/Auto flips <html data-theme="dark-theme"> itself — every DS token switches, the choice persists to localStorage, and Auto follows the OS. Set false to make the switcher emit-only (the app applies the theme via the `theme` event).

events.name: select
events.note: an account link was clicked; payload is its key/label (detail[0]).

events.name: theme
events.note: the theme segment changed; the consumer applies the scheme (dark/light or system-auto).

decisionFlow: The header account control (avatar -> profile links + theme + Logout)? -> obs-user-menu, in the obs-app-header `user` slot.
A generic row-of-actions menu (Edit / Delete on a grid row)? -> obs-menu (context), NOT obs-user-menu.
Navigating between modules/sections? -> obs-sidebar / obs-side-menu, NOT a user menu.
Have a user photo? -> set `avatar` (src); else it shows `initials` (derived from `name`).
Avatar on the left of its container? -> placement="bottom-start".

default.useWhen: the standard app-shell account menu — avatar + name/email header, account links, theme toggle, Logout
default.dontUse: for a generic action menu (obs-menu) or navigation (obs-sidebar)
default.example: obs-app-header `user` slot: My Profile / Product Setup Guide / Documentation / Dark theme / Logout

avatar-image.useWhen: the user has a profile photo
avatar-image.dontUse: no photo — initials read fine and avoid a broken image

minimal.useWhen: an embedded/restricted account menu with just links
minimal.dontUse: the standard shell (users expect the theme toggle + Logout)

theme-switcher.useWhen: the app offers per-user Dark / Light / Auto — the switcher belongs in the account menu (the product pattern)
theme-switcher.dontUse: the app has a single fixed theme (theme-toggle="false"); or a global theme control lives elsewhere
theme-switcher.example: theme="auto" → the Auto segment is active; changing it emits theme:{value} for the consumer to apply

placement-start.useWhen: the avatar is positioned so a right-aligned dropdown would overflow — anchor it left
placement-start.dontUse: the standard top-right chrome (bottom-end is correct there)

theme-toggle.useWhen: you want the account menu to switch the whole UI theme — it works out of the box (no wiring): Dark/Light/Auto flips the document and persists.
theme-toggle.dontUse: the host app already owns theming — then set manage-theme="false" and handle the `theme` event yourself.
theme-toggle.must: leave manage-theme on by default so anything built with the DS gets a working theme switch; Auto follows the OS.
theme-toggle.example: <obs-user-menu name="Nirav" theme-toggle></obs-user-menu> → Dark/Light/Auto immediately theme the page.

usage.note: One per app shell (the header account control). Turnkey element for the user-menu recipe.

do: Place it in obs-app-header's `user` slot (the top-right of the shell).
Wire the `logout` event to the sign-out flow and `theme` to your data-theme toggle.
Keep the link list short — profile, setup/help, docs; deep settings live in the sidebar.
Give the avatar meaningful initials (derived from name) or a real photo.
dont: Don't use it as a generic action menu — that's obs-menu.
Don't stuff navigation into it (modules live in obs-sidebar).
Don't hardcode colours — the danger Logout uses --secondary-red, rows use tokens.

a11y.summary: The avatar is a button with aria-label "Account menu" + aria-expanded. The dropdown is a role=menu of menuitem rows; it opens in the top layer, closes on click-outside and Esc. The danger Logout is distinguished by an icon + red, not colour alone.
a11y.notes: Focus: move focus into the panel on open and back to the avatar on close for full keyboard support (the element wires Esc + click-outside; consumers should ensure the rows are tab-reachable). Announce the theme change (aria-live). The avatar needs a discernible name — initials alone are fine because the trigger carries aria-label.

knownIssues: The theme switcher emits `theme` {value} (dark/light/auto) but does NOT itself apply the scheme — the consumer sets data-theme / follows the system for auto (kept app-agnostic). Reuses the product moon/sun/theme-auto glyphs (added to the icon library).
changelog: 2026-08-06 — Theme switcher is now BUILT-IN + functional (owner): selecting Dark/Light/Auto flips <html data-theme="dark-theme"> itself (matches the DS CSS + showcase), persists the choice to localStorage, and Auto follows prefers-color-scheme — no consumer wiring needed. Added the manage-theme prop (default true; false = emit-only) + usageRule. Anything built with the DS gets a working theme switch out of the box.
